opening: Background: The discovery that gut microbial dysbiosis correlated with prognosis, immune reconstitution and development of graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) in patients undergoing allogeneic stem cell transplantation (allo-SCT) highlights the clinical relevance of the gut microbiome in shaping anti-tumor immune responses. Treatment of allo-SCT patients with antibiotics has recently been associated with increased GVHD mortality (Routy et al. 2017). Based on these studies and the association of distinct gut bacteria with increased efficacy to PD-1 blockade in patients with solid tumors (Derosa et al. sociation of distinct gut bacteria with increased efficacy to PD-1 blockade in patients with solid tumors (Derosa et al. 2018), we performed a retrospective analysis to determine if infection treated with antibiotics affected the outcomes of multiple myeloma (MM) patients after autologous SCT (ASCT). Methods: A list of all MM patients treated at our institution between January 2012 through December 2015 was obtained and 1095 patients were identified.
